newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament rejects new Ciller graft probe.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament rejects new Ciller graft probe.

text.p: The Turkish parliament on Tuesday decided against setting up a new inquiry into Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller that could have send her to the Supreme Court on corruption charges.

Deputy speaker Yasin Hatipoglu said MPs voted 247 to 242 to reject an opposition proposal to probe allegations that Ciller was involved in corruption at the state-owned Turban hotel and tourism company.
The vote could have caused a rift in the Islamist-led coalition government if it had gone against Ciller, also the foreign minister.
Ciller recently avoided being sent to the Supreme Court in three alleged corruption cases with the help of MPs from her Welfare Party government ally who voted to drop the charges.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare again backed Ciller in the Turban vote.

The latest accusations date back to Ciller's three years as Turkey's first woman prime minister from 1993. They include claims that Ciller blocked the prosecution of Turban's former boss, now an MP in her True Path Party, on corruption charges.
The main opposition Motherland Party also says Ciller used Turban's hotel and yacht marine facilities for personal purposes and that company employees did work at the Ciller family's farm.
Pro-Western secularist Ciller formed a coalition last June that made Erbakan the first Islamist leader in Turkey's modern history.
